frontHtml: Myocardial oxygen supply and demand: The left ventricle extracts about 70–75% of the oxygen delivered to it even at rest, so a rise in demand is met almost entirely by a rise in […], not by more extraction.
backHtml: The left ventricle extracts about 70–75% of the oxygen delivered to it even at rest, so a rise in demand is met almost entirely by a rise in coronary blood flow, not by more extraction.

frontHtml: Myocardial oxygen supply and demand: Flow to the left ventricle occurs mostly in […], when the contracting wall no longer compresses intramural vessels.
backHtml: Flow to the left ventricle occurs mostly in diastole, when the contracting wall no longer compresses intramural vessels.

frontHtml: Explain why increased myocardial oxygen demand is met by increased coronary flow rather than increased extraction.
backHtml: the heart raises supply by raising flow, not extraction.

frontHtml: Calculate the number needed to treat from two event rates.
Choose primary PCI for STEMI when it is promptly available.
backHtml: In ST-elevation myocardial infarction, primary PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy when it can be performed promptly (within 120 minutes of first medical contact).

frontHtml: Treat hypotension from right ventricular infarction with volume.
backHtml: Right ventricular infarction makes cardiac output preload-dependent.
